title: Flat Tag Identity Delivery
summary: migrate namespaced canonical tags, assignments, aliases, services, and UI to globally unique flat tag names and remove group-dependent behavior
content_html:
Flat Tag Identity Delivery

Complete Result

Studio reads, assigns, creates, edits, deletes, promotes, and demotes canonical tags using globally unique flat IDs such as moss.

No canonical tag source, assignment, alias rule, service contract, runtime configuration, route, or analysis behavior treats group as tag data. Registry descriptions remain temporarily available, including the results of manual collision editing, so Tag-document linking can transfer them into documents.

The transitional registry record after this delivery is:

{
  "tag_id": "moss",
  "description": "<temporary document seed content>",
  "updated_at_utc": "<timestamp>"
}

Migration Gate

Before mechanical migration, manually resolve the current 19 labels that have more than one namespaced registry row.

For each collision, decide:

  • the one resulting flat tag_id;
  • the combined or rewritten registry description retained for document seeding;
  • assignment references that collapse to the flat ID;
  • alias targets and historical selection context; and
  • whether any genuinely different concept needs a genuinely different name.

Keep the reviewed decisions in a temporary migration artifact owned by this delivery. Do not infer them from matching labels or descriptions.

In Scope

  • Change canonical registry identity from <group>:<slug> to one globally unique normalized tag name.
  • Remove singular group, any redundant label that only repeats tag_id, allowed-group policy, and the canonical tag-group taxonomy source.
  • Preserve one registry description per resulting tag as temporary semantic source for Tag-document linking.
  • Migrate canonical series and work assignment references without changing their series-first ownership or override semantics.
  • Migrate alias targets and historical selection context; remove one-target-per- group constraints and group selection from promotion and demotion.
  • Update first-class create, edit, rename, delete, promotion, demotion, validation, transaction, rollback, activity, and manual-patch behavior.
  • Remove group filtering, ordering, chips, styling, configuration, group routes, group coverage/scoring, and group-derived analytics.
  • Update focused services, APIs, frontend modules, audits, checks, and tests to the flat identity contract.

Not In Scope

  • Creating, linking, editing, or publishing tag documents.
  • Adding doc_id to the registry or removing registry description.
  • Replacing group with groups, categories, facets, senses, namespaces, or a compatibility prefix.
  • Inferring collision outcomes automatically.
  • Changing catalogue membership or the series/work assignment ownership model.
  • Adding Tag semantic-token targets.

Likely Authority

  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-aliases.json
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-assignments.json
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-groups.json
  • Studio tag runtime configuration and activity contracts
  • studio/services/tags/
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-*
  • studio/app/frontend/js/analytics-tag-*
  • Series Tags and Series Tag Editor frontend owners
  • tag consistency audits and focused registry, alias, assignment, route, and browser-boundary tests

These are inspection starting points. Confirm all consumers of namespaced IDs, group fields, and group-derived configuration before editing canonical data.

Completion And Evidence

  • Every canonical registry row has one unique flat tag_id and no group field.
  • All registry descriptions needed by the next feature survive under the manually resolved flat identities.
  • Every canonical assignment and alias target resolves to a current flat tag.
  • No executable path parses a tag ID prefix to recover group.
  • No executable tag workflow reads or writes group policy, group taxonomy, or group-derived analytical state.
  • New Tag and promotion create flat IDs without a group choice.
  • Rename, delete, demotion, and assignment writes preserve their existing cross-file planning, atomic replacement, rollback, and activity guarantees.
  • Focused model/planner/API tests, route/module checks, exact canonical-data reconciliation, scoped source searches, a manual UI pass, and git diff --check support only this bounded migration.

Durable Destination

Update Tag Source Data, Tag Registry, Tag Aliases, Series Tags, and Series Tag Editor with the shipped flat identity contract.

Tag Groups becomes a closeout retirement candidate after its executable taxonomy owner is removed; retirement still requires the normal explicit review and confirmation.
